# AppSync GraphQL and Events

Run GraphQL APIs with local resolvers and Event APIs with HTTP publishing and WebSocket subscriptions.

**Status: implemented subset.** Operation selection does not imply complete input or behavior parity.

| Contract | Current implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Service ID | `appsync` |
| Signing name | `appsync` |
| Wire protocol | REST JSON |
| API version | `2017-07-25` |
| Scope | Account and region |
| Execution | Local behavior |
| Selected operations | 46 of 74 in the pinned model |

## Implemented behavior

See the [implemented feature catalogue](catalogue.md#appsync-graphql-and-events) for this service's capabilities.

## Limitations and future work

- JavaScript utilities and VTL form a local subset of AppSync runtimes.
- Subscriptions live in memory and close on shutdown.
- Event handlerConfigs, direct data source integrations, S3-hosted handlers and logging configuration are rejected.
- Event subscriptions are transient; API, namespace, handler and key records survive sqlite restarts.
- Event authorization updates apply immediately; Lambda authorization results are not cached.
- Production scaling, caching and every upstream resolver/data-source option are not reproduced.
- Reset keeps real-time WebSocket connections and their subscriptions.
- The console has no query runner: the API Gateway InvokeApi action is service-specific and there is no shared AppSync data-plane proxy. GraphQL API records expose no creation timestamp.

These gaps describe current boundaries and possible follow-up slices. The [roadmap](../roadmap/index.md)
separates proposed work from registered functionality; there are no promised release dates.
